digital_arrest.title: Fake Digital Arrest / CBI Scam
digital_arrest.description: Fraudsters posing as Police/CBI on a video call, claiming your Aadhaar or parcel is linked to illegal activities and demanding money to avoid 'digital arrest'.
actions: DISCONNECT the call immediately. Real police DO NOT arrest via Skype or WhatsApp.
Understand: THERE IS NO CONCEPT OF 'DIGITAL ARREST' IN INDIAN LAW.
Do NOT transfer any money to 'verify' your accounts or as a 'security deposit'.
Call the National Cyber Crime Helpline (1930) to report the numbers and accounts.
tips: Never accept unsolicited video calls from unknown numbers.
Government agencies do not ask for money transfers to clear your name.
Do not share your screen or download any apps they suggest.

investment_scam.title: Fake Investment / Trading Scam
investment_scam.description: Lured into WhatsApp or Telegram groups offering stock tips or crypto investments, leading to massive financial loss through fake trading apps.
actions: Stop depositing any more money, even if they say it's a 'withdrawal tax' or 'fee'.
Take screenshots of all chats, group members, and bank transfer receipts.
Call 1930 immediately and block the destination bank accounts.
Report the specific fake app or website link on the cybercrime portal.
tips: SEBI-registered brokers do not operate via informal WhatsApp or Telegram groups.
If returns sound too good to be true, it is a scam.
Never download trading apps from unknown APK links; use official app stores.

loan_app.title: Loan App Harassment
loan_app.description: Downloaded an instant loan app that stole your contacts and gallery, and is now morphing photos and blackmailing you.
actions: Do NOT pay them. Paying once will only lead to more blackmail.
Uninstall the fraudulent app immediately and revoke all permissions.
Inform your close contacts that your phone was hacked and to ignore fake messages.
File a complaint at the nearest cyber police station or on the national portal.
tips: Only borrow from RBI-registered NBFCs or banks.
Never grant 'Contacts' or 'Gallery' permissions to unverified loan apps.
Check the app publisher details and reviews before downloading.

upi_scam.title: UPI / Digital Payment Fraud
upi_scam.description: Lost money through a fake UPI payment request, OTP scam, or malicious APK banking app.
actions: Immediately call the National Cyber Crime Helpline (1930).
Contact your bank to block your account/card and dispute the transaction.
Register a formal complaint on the official cybercrime portal.
Take screenshots of the transaction ID and messages.
tips: Never share OTPs or PINs with anyone.
Do not click on unverified payment links.
Verify the receiver's name before entering your UPI PIN.

voice_scam.title: Fake Bank / KYC Call Scam
voice_scam.description: Received a call claiming your bank account, SIM, or electricity will be blocked unless you update KYC immediately.
actions: Disconnect the call. Do not follow any instructions to download apps (like AnyDesk/TeamViewer).
Do not share any OTPs received during the call.
Call your bank or service provider using the official number from their website.
Report the fraudulent number on the Chakshu portal (Sanchar Saathi).
tips: Banks and telecom operators NEVER ask you to download screen-sharing apps.
Do not panic. Official disconnections require formal written notices, not sudden phone calls.
Use caller ID apps to spot frequently reported scam numbers.

qr_code_scam.title: QR Code Scam
qr_code_scam.description: Asked to scan a QR code on OLX or WhatsApp to receive money, but money was deducted instead.
actions: Contact your bank immediately to block the transaction and your account.
Call the National Cyber Crime Helpline (1930).
Take screenshots of the QR code and chat history with the scammer.
Report the incident on the cybercrime portal.
tips: You NEVER need to enter your UPI PIN or scan a QR code to RECEIVE money.
Be wary of buyers on platforms like OLX insisting on paying via QR code.
Verify the identity of the person you are transacting with.

account_hacked.title: Social Media Account Hacked
account_hacked.description: If your social media account (Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp) is compromised or impersonated.
actions: Use the platform's official account recovery page.
Do NOT pay any ransom if demanded by the hacker.
Warn your contacts not to respond to messages from your account.
Report the impersonation/hack on the cybercrime portal.
tips: Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA).
Do not click on suspicious links sent in DMs.
Use strong, unique passwords for every platform.

lost_phone.title: Lost or Stolen Mobile Device
lost_phone.description: If your smartphone is lost or stolen, putting your data and finances at risk.
actions: Block your SIM card immediately by contacting your telecom provider.
File an FIR at the nearest police station.
Use the CEIR portal to block your device's IMEI number.
Remotely wipe your data using Google Find My Device or Apple Find My.
tips: Always keep a record of your phone's IMEI number (*#06#).
Enable 'Find My Device' on your phone.
Set a strong lock screen PIN/Password.

sextortion.title: Sextortion / Blackmail
sextortion.description: If you are being blackmailed with intimate images or videos by scammers.
actions: Do NOT pay any money to the extortionists; they will only demand more.
Block all communication and do not answer further calls/messages.
Take screenshots of the threats, profiles, and phone numbers.
Report immediately to the Cyber Crime Portal.
tips: Do not accept video calls from unknown numbers.
Maintain strict privacy settings on social media.
Do not share intimate images online.

fake_shopping.title: E-Commerce Fraud / Fake Product
fake_shopping.description: Paid for a product but received nothing, a counterfeit product, or got a stone in the package.
actions: Record an unboxing video if you suspect the package.
Contact the e-commerce platform's support immediately.
Contact your bank to initiate a chargeback for the transaction.
File a grievance on the National Consumer Helpline portal.
tips: Buy only from trusted, verified sellers and platforms.
Read seller reviews and ratings before purchasing.
Always take an unboxing video for expensive items.

banking_fraud.title: Banking Service Fraud / Dispute
banking_fraud.description: ATM cash not dispensed but deducted, hidden bank charges, or unauthorized credit card transactions.
actions: Immediately report unauthorized transactions to your bank to limit liability.
For failed ATM transactions, file a complaint with the card-issuing bank within 30 days.
If the bank rejects your claim unjustly, file a complaint with the Banking Ombudsman (RBI).
tips: Check your bank statements regularly for hidden fees.
Never share your credit card CVV or PIN.
Set transaction limits on your debit/credit cards via your banking app.

telecom_issue.title: Telecom / Network Complaints
telecom_issue.description: Persistent call drops, wrong billing, or recharge issues without resolution from the provider.
actions: Lodge a formal complaint with the telecom operator's appellate authority.
Keep records of complaint numbers and emails.
If unresolved within 30 days, file a grievance on the PGPORTAL or NCH.
tips: Read post-paid billing plans carefully to avoid hidden data charges.
Use official apps for recharges to avoid third-party failures.

real_estate.title: Real Estate / Builder Fraud
real_estate.description: Delayed flat possession, fake amenities promised, or builder absconding with funds.
actions: Gather all payment receipts, builder agreements, and brochures.
File a formal complaint with your state's Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA).
Form an association with other affected buyers for stronger legal standing.
Lodge a case in the Consumer Court for deficiency of service.
tips: Only invest in RERA-registered projects and check the RERA website for project status.
Never pay large sums in cash.
Have a lawyer review the builder-buyer agreement before signing.

healthcare.title: Healthcare & Insurance Claims
healthcare.description: Unfairly rejected health insurance claims or hidden/excessive hospital charges.
actions: Request a written, detailed denial letter from the TPA/Insurance company.
Escalate the grievance to the insurance company's Grievance Redressal Officer.
If unresolved within 15 days, file a complaint with the Insurance Ombudsman.
File a complaint on the National Consumer Helpline for hospital overcharging.
tips: Read the exclusions and waiting periods in your insurance policy document.
Disclose all pre-existing medical conditions truthfully when buying insurance.
Ask hospitals for an itemized bill before payment.

refund_denied.title: Refund Denied Unfairly
refund_denied.description: If an e-commerce platform or seller refuses to refund your money for a valid return or canceled order.
actions: Keep all email and chat transcripts with the seller/platform.
Send a formal email threatening to escalate to consumer court.
File a chargeback request with your credit card company or bank.
Lodge a complaint on the National Consumer Helpline.
tips: Always read the return/refund policy before making a purchase.
Prefer platforms with clearly stated, customer-friendly return policies.
Keep proof of dispatch when returning an item.

digital_arrest_cbi.title: The CBI Video Call
digital_arrest_cbi.description: You receive a Skype video call from someone claiming to be a CBI officer threatening you with 'digital arrest'.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You get an automated call saying a parcel in your name was seized. The call is transferred to 'CBI', and they ask you to join a Skype video call.

decision_1.title: What is your immediate next step?
decision_1.content: The 'officer' warns you not to disconnect or tell your family. He asks you to transfer your bank balance to an 'RBI secure account'.

options.label: Transfer the money to prove your innocence.
Disconnect the call immediately and call 1930.

result_wrong_1.title: Incorrect Action
result_wrong_1.content: You have fallen for the 'Digital Arrest' scam. Indian law has NO concept of digital arrest.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: You avoided a major scam! Real police do not interrogate or arrest via Skype.

digital_arrest_customs.title: The Customs Parcel Trap
digital_arrest_customs.description: An automated call claims FedEx or Customs has blocked your parcel.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You receive an IVR call saying 'This is FedEx. A parcel sent from your name to Taiwan has been intercepted. Press 1 to speak to Customs.'

decision_1.title: What do you do?
decision_1.content: You haven't sent any parcel to Taiwan.

options.label: Press 1 to clarify it wasn't you.

result_wrong_1.title: You're Being Reeled In
result_wrong_1.content: By pressing 1, you are connected to a scammer who will now use fear tactics.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Good job. Official couriers do not use automated IVR calls to threaten you.

digital_arrest_aadhaar.title: The Aadhaar Threat
digital_arrest_aadhaar.description: A caller claims your Aadhaar is linked to money laundering.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: A caller identifies themselves as an official from the 'Telecom Department'. They claim 5 illegal SIM cards were purchased using your Aadhaar.

decision_1.title: They ask for your Aadhaar OTP to 'verify and block' the SIMs.
decision_1.content: They threaten police action if you don't cooperate.

options.label: Give the OTP to block the illegal SIMs.
Hang up and check the TAFCOP portal.

result_wrong_1.title: Identity Compromised
result_wrong_1.content: You just gave them access to your Aadhaar authentication. Never share an OTP.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Government officials will never ask for an OTP over the phone.

upi_urgent_request.title: The Urgent Request
upi_urgent_request.description: A friend urgently requests money via WhatsApp from an unknown number.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You receive a WhatsApp message from an unknown number. The profile picture is your close friend, asking for ₹10,000 urgently.

decision_1.title: What do you do?
decision_1.content: The person is pressuring you.

options.label: Call your friend on their original number.

result_wrong_1.title: Incorrect Action
result_wrong_1.content: Fraudsters use stolen profile pictures to impersonate contacts.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Always verify urgent requests by calling the person's known number.

upi_qr_scam.title: The OLX QR Code Trap
upi_qr_scam.description: A buyer insists on sending you money via a QR code.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: An OLX buyer agrees to your price but insists on paying via a QR code they just sent you on WhatsApp.

decision_1.title: They ask you to scan it.
decision_1.content: The message says 'Scan to Receive ₹5,000'.

options.label: Refuse. Tell them to send via phone number.

result_wrong_1.title: Money Deducted!
result_wrong_1.content: Scanning a QR code is ONLY for SENDING money. You never scan to receive money.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: You spotted the scam. UPI PIN is NEVER required to receive money.

upi_customer_care.title: The Fake Helpline
upi_customer_care.description: You call a customer care number found on Google.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You search 'Swiggy Customer Care' on Google. The executive asks you to download 'AnyDesk' to process a refund.

decision_1.title: What do you do?
decision_1.content: They claim it's standard RBI protocol.

result_wrong_1.title: Total Compromise
result_wrong_1.content: AnyDesk is a screen-sharing app. The scammer can now see your banking PINs.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Always use the official app's help section, never Google Search numbers.

fake_product_stone.title: Stone in the Parcel
fake_product_stone.description: You ordered an iPhone but received a stone.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You open your newly delivered smartphone box and find a brick inside.

decision_1.title: Immediate next step?
decision_1.content: You are in shock.

options.label: Record video of box/labels and contact support.

result_wrong_1.title: Not Enough Evidence
result_wrong_1.content: Without an unboxing video, platforms may reject your claim.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Evidence is crucial. Always take photos of tampered seals and labels.

fake_product_empty.title: The Empty Envelope
fake_product_empty.description: You paid for clothes but received paper.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You bought dresses from an Instagram store. A courier arrives with a flat envelope containing blank paper.

decision_1.title: Why did they do this?
decision_1.content: The Instagram page blocked you.

options.label: To generate a valid 'Delivered' tracking receipt.

result_wrong_1.title: It's a Scam
result_wrong_1.content: This is 'Empty Tracking Fraud'.

result_correct_1.title: Correct!
result_correct_1.content: Scammers use the tracking proof to deny your bank chargeback.

fake_product_different.title: The Bait and Switch
fake_product_different.description: You ordered a branded jacket but received a knockoff.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You pay Cash on Delivery for Nike shoes but receive unbranded plastic shoes.

decision_1.title: Who do you hold responsible?
decision_1.content: The website disappeared.

options.label: The logistics company handling the COD.

result_wrong_1.title: Misplaced Blame
result_wrong_1.content: The delivery boy doesn't know what's inside and can't refund you directly.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Contact the courier's grievance officer to freeze the COD remittance.

loan_app_scenario.title: The Instant Loan Threat
loan_app_scenario.description: An instant loan app starts blackmailing you.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You repaid an instant loan, but they demand ₹50,000 more and threaten to send morphed photos to your contacts.

decision_1.title: How do you handle it?
decision_1.content: They start a 10-minute timer.

options.label: Do NOT pay. Uninstall and warn contacts.

result_wrong_1.title: The Trap Closes
result_wrong_1.content: Extortionists never stop. They will demand more tomorrow.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Never pay. Warning your contacts pre-emptively removes their leverage.

voice_scam_disconnect.title: Electricity Bill Threat
voice_scam_disconnect.description: A message threatens to cut your power tonight.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You get an SMS: 'Dear consumer, your power will be disconnected at 9:30 PM. Call this number to update bills.'

decision_1.title: What do you do?
decision_1.content: It's 8:00 PM and you are panicked.

result_wrong_1.title: Scam Initiated
result_wrong_1.content: Calling connects you to a scammer who will ask you to download a screen-sharing app to 'pay a ₹10 fee'.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Electricity boards do not send threatening personal SMS messages from 10-digit mobile numbers.

voice_scam_kyc.title: The Pan Card KYC Update
voice_scam_kyc.description: A caller claims your bank account will be frozen without a PAN update.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: A caller says your HDFC account needs an urgent PAN link via a link sent to your SMS.

decision_1.title: Do you click the link?
decision_1.content: The link looks like 'hdfc-kyc-update.com'.

result_wrong_1.title: Phishing Trap
result_wrong_1.content: The link is fake. Entering details gives hackers access to your banking.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Banks never ask you to update KYC via random SMS links.

hack_insta.title: Instagram Investment Scam
hack_insta.description: Your friend posts about huge crypto profits.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: Your friend's Instagram posts a story: 'I just made $5000 in 2 hours! DM me to learn how.'

decision_1.title: What do you do?
decision_1.content: You DM them and they ask for a $100 deposit.

result_wrong_1.title: Account Hacked
result_wrong_1.content: Your friend's account was hacked. You just paid a scammer.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Calling confirms their account was compromised. Good job.

hack_whatsapp.title: The WhatsApp Verification Code
hack_whatsapp.description: Someone asks you to forward a 6-digit code.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: A friend messages: 'Hey, I accidentally sent my login code to your number. Can you send it back?'

decision_1.title: Do you forward the SMS code you just received?
decision_1.content: The SMS says 'WhatsApp Registration Code'.

result_wrong_1.title: WhatsApp Hacked
result_wrong_1.content: That was YOUR login code. The scammer just hijacked your WhatsApp account.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Never forward 6-digit codes to anyone, even known contacts.

lost_phone_otp.title: Stolen Phone OTP Risk
lost_phone_otp.description: Your phone is stolen while unlocked.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: A thief snatched your phone from your hand while it was unlocked and you were reading an article.

decision_1.title: What is your FIRST priority?
decision_1.content: The thief has access to everything.

options.label: Block your SIM and bank apps.

result_wrong_1.title: Too Slow
result_wrong_1.content: By the time the FIR is filed, the thief will reset your UPI pin using OTPs and drain your accounts.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Blocking the SIM stops OTPs. This must happen within minutes.

lost_phone_extortion.title: The 'Find My iPhone' Phishing
lost_phone_extortion.description: Thieves try to get your iCloud password.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: Days after your iPhone is stolen, you receive an SMS: 'Your lost iPhone was found. Click here to view location: apple-support-find.com'

decision_1.title: Do you click and log in?
decision_1.content: You really want your phone back.

result_wrong_1.title: Device Unlocked
result_wrong_1.content: It was a phishing link. You just gave the thieves your iCloud password, allowing them to wipe and sell the phone.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Thieves send fake Apple/Google links to get your password. Never click them.

sextortion_video.title: The Unknown Video Call
sextortion_video.description: You answer a WhatsApp video call from a stranger.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You answer a video call from an unknown number. The screen shows an explicit video, and they record your face reacting to it.

decision_1.title: They threaten to post the recording to YouTube unless you pay ₹20,000.
decision_1.content: What do you do?

options.label: Pay the money out of fear.

result_wrong_1.title: Endless Extortion
result_wrong_1.content: Paying marks you as a lucrative target. They will demand more money tomorrow.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Scammers mass-call people. If you block them and refuse to pay, they usually move on to the next victim.

sextortion_morph.title: Morphed Photo Threat
sextortion_morph.description: Someone morphs your public Facebook photos.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: A scammer takes your public Facebook profile picture, morphs it onto an explicit image, and sends it to your Messenger.

decision_1.title: They demand Amazon Gift Cards to delete it.
decision_1.content: What do you do?

options.label: Lock your profile and report to 1930.

result_wrong_1.title: You Paid a Scammer
result_wrong_1.content: They will just morph another photo. You cannot buy your way out of extortion.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Locking down your privacy settings and reporting to cybercrime is the only way to handle morphing threats.

bank_atm_fail.title: ATM Cash Not Dispensed
bank_atm_fail.description: The ATM doesn't give cash but your account is debited.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You try to withdraw ₹10,000. The machine makes a noise, gives an error, but you get an SMS saying money was deducted.

decision_1.title: When do you complain?
decision_1.content: The bank branch is currently closed.

options.label: Wait a week to see if it reverses.
Call customer care and raise a dispute immediately.

result_wrong_1.title: Too Late
result_wrong_1.content: Banks have a strict time window (usually 30 days) for ATM disputes. Waiting risks your money.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Always log a complaint immediately. If the bank doesn't resolve it in 30 days, you can approach the RBI Ombudsman.

bank_card_swipe.title: Unauthorized Credit Card Swipe
bank_card_swipe.description: Your card is swiped for a large amount in another country.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You wake up to an SMS: 'USD 500 spent on your Credit Card in London.' Your card is physically with you.

decision_1.title: What must you do to ensure zero liability?
decision_1.content: You must act fast.

options.label: Report it to the bank within 3 days.
Cancel the card via the app and forget it.

result_wrong_1.title: You Still Owe Money
result_wrong_1.content: Canceling the card doesn't reverse the charge. You must officially report the fraud.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Under RBI rules, if you report unauthorized electronic transactions within 3 working days, your liability is ZERO.

telecom_sim_block.title: Unfair SIM Deactivation
telecom_sim_block.description: Your primary number is suddenly deactivated.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: Your Jio SIM suddenly stops working. Customer care says it was deactivated due to non-usage, but you recharged it last month.

decision_1.title: Where do you escalate?
decision_1.content: The store executive refuses to help.

result_wrong_1.title: Wrong Venue
result_wrong_1.content: Police don't handle telecom billing disputes.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Telecom operators have a structured grievance process ending with the Appellate Authority. Use it.

telecom_bill_shock.title: Postpaid Bill Shock
telecom_bill_shock.description: You receive a bill for ₹15,000 due to roaming.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You get your Airtel postpaid bill. It's ₹15,000 because 'International Roaming' was activated without your consent.

decision_1.title: Do you have to pay?
decision_1.content: The company threatens to ruin your CIBIL score.

options.label: Pay it to protect your credit score.
Dispute it via PGPORTAL or Consumer Helpline.

result_wrong_1.title: Lost Money
result_wrong_1.content: If you didn't opt-in, it's an unfair trade practice. Paying it means you accept the charge.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Companies cannot activate premium services without explicit consent. Dispute it officially.

real_estate_delay.title: Builder Possession Delay
real_estate_delay.description: The builder is 3 years late on delivering your flat.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You paid 80% for an under-construction flat. The handover date passed 3 years ago, and construction has stopped.

decision_1.title: What is your best legal remedy?
decision_1.content: You are paying both rent and EMI.

result_wrong_1.title: Financial Ruin
result_wrong_1.content: Stopping EMI hurts YOUR credit score, not the builder. The bank will seize your assets.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: RERA tribunals are specifically set up to force builders to pay delay penalties or refund buyers.

real_estate_amenities.title: Fake Amenities Promised
real_estate_amenities.description: The brochure showed a pool, but there is none.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You move into your new flat. The builder's brochure promised a swimming pool and gym, but the space was sold as parking instead.

decision_1.title: Can you take action?
decision_1.content: The builder says the brochure was 'indicative'.

options.label: Yes, it's an unfair trade practice.

result_wrong_1.title: Incorrect
result_wrong_1.content: Consumer courts have repeatedly ruled that brochures and advertisements are binding promises.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: File a joint complaint with other residents in the Consumer Court for compensation.

health_claim_denied.title: Cashless Claim Denied
health_claim_denied.description: Your health insurance refuses to pay during an emergency.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: Your father is hospitalized. You present your valid health insurance card, but the TPA rejects the cashless claim citing 'unjustified hospitalization'.

decision_1.title: What do you do?
decision_1.content: The hospital is demanding a ₹2 Lakh deposit.

options.label: Pay, collect all bills, and file for reimbursement.

result_wrong_1.title: Waste of Time
result_wrong_1.content: The hospital cannot control the TPA's decision. Arguing delays medical care.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Pay for the treatment, ensure you get detailed medical justifications from the doctor, and file for reimbursement. If denied again, approach the Insurance Ombudsman.

health_hidden_charge.title: Hospital Overcharging
health_hidden_charge.description: You are billed ₹50,000 for 'miscellaneous medical supplies'.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: Upon discharge, the hospital gives you a final bill. You notice ₹50,000 lumped under 'admin charges and miscellaneous supplies'.

decision_1.title: How do you handle the bill?
decision_1.content: They won't let you leave without paying.

options.label: Demand an itemized bill before paying.

result_wrong_1.title: Lost Money
result_wrong_1.content: Hospitals often inflate generic charges. You should always demand transparency.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: You have a legal right to an itemized bill. Threatening to file a complaint on the Consumer Helpline often gets these padded charges removed.

refund_policy_trap.title: The 'No Refunds' Policy
refund_policy_trap.description: A gym refuses to refund you for unused months.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You paid for a 1-year gym membership but had to relocate after 1 month. The gym refuses to refund the remaining 11 months, pointing to a 'No Refunds' sign.

decision_1.title: Is their 'No Refunds' sign legally valid?
decision_1.content: They made you sign a contract saying the same.

result_wrong_1.title: Incorrect
result_wrong_1.content: Consumer Protection laws override unfair business contracts.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Courts view non-refundable clauses for unrendered services as 'Unfair Trade Practices'. You can file a grievance to get a pro-rata refund.

refund_delay_scam.title: The 7-14 Business Days Loop
refund_delay_scam.description: An airline keeps delaying your refund.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: An airline canceled your flight. They promised a refund in '7-14 business days'. It has been 45 days, and customer care just keeps repeating the same script.

decision_1.title: What is your best move?
decision_1.content: You paid via Credit Card.

options.label: Initiate a chargeback with your credit card company.

result_wrong_1.title: Wasted Time
result_wrong_1.content: Customer care agents have no power to release funds stuck in accounting loops.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: A 'Services Not Rendered' chargeback dispute through your bank forces the merchant to prove they provided the service, bypassing their customer care entirely.

invest_whatsapp.title: WhatsApp Stock Tips
invest_whatsapp.description: You are added to a WhatsApp group promising 300% returns on stocks.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: A random number adds you to a 'VIP Stock Traders' group. Everyone is posting screenshots of huge profits.

decision_1.title: The admin asks you to download their 'custom trading app' to get started.
decision_1.content: What do you do?

options.label: Leave the group and block the admin.

result_wrong_1.title: It's a Fake Dashboard
result_wrong_1.content: The app is fake. The numbers will go up, but you will never be able to withdraw your money.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: SEBI-registered brokers do not operate via WhatsApp groups or custom APKs. It's a classic scam.

invest_crypto.title: The Crypto Romance
invest_crypto.description: Someone you met on a dating app suggests a crypto investment.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You matched with someone attractive on Tinder. After 2 weeks of chatting, they say they made a fortune in crypto and want to teach you.

decision_1.title: They send you a link to a 'secret trading platform'.
decision_1.content: They promise it's risk-free.

options.label: Transfer a small amount to try.

result_wrong_1.title: Pig Butchering Scam
result_wrong_1.content: They 'fatten' you up with fake profits on a fake site, then steal everything. This is a global scam.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Never take financial advice from strangers on dating apps or social media.

loan_app_harassment.title: 7-Day Loan Contact Abuse
loan_app_harassment.description: A loan app creates a WhatsApp group with your family members.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You missed the 7-day deadline for an instant loan. The app automatically creates a WhatsApp group named 'Defaulter' and adds your parents and boss.

decision_1.title: They send abusive messages to the group.
decision_1.content: What do you do?

options.label: Beg them in the group and promise to pay.
Post a message saying your phone was hacked, then exit.

result_wrong_1.title: Public Humiliation
result_wrong_1.content: Begging shows weakness. They will demand 3x the loan amount to stop the harassment.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Damage control is key. Informing contacts it's a hack removes their leverage, then report to cyber police.

qr_fake_payment.title: The Spoofed Audio Box
qr_fake_payment.description: A customer shows you a fake payment success screen.

intro.title: The Situation
intro.content: You run a small shop. A customer buys goods worth ₹500, scans your QR code, and shows you a screen saying 'Payment Successful'.

decision_1.title: Your payment soundbox didn't announce the payment.
decision_1.content: The customer is in a hurry.

options.label: Let them go, the screen looked real.
Make them wait until you receive an SMS or soundbox alert.

result_wrong_1.title: Spoofed Screen
result_wrong_1.content: There are fake apps that generate exact replicas of Paytm/GPay success screens. You lost your money.

result_correct_1.title: Correct Action!
result_correct_1.content: Never trust a screenshot or the customer's phone. Only trust your own bank SMS or payment audio box.
